question: Will Ukraine have de facto control of Dobropillia, Donetsk on December 31, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo: ISW assesses no consolidated Russian positions in Dobropillia; nearest assessed advances ~5 km from the admin building as of Nov 7; only ~6 weeks remain. Reference class: Russian assaults on defended Donbas towns of 20k+ (Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, Chasiv Yar) took many months from ~5 km to ISW center control. Polymarket 'capture Dobropillia' prices Nov 30 <1% and Mar 31 2027 ~43% ($158K vol), implying roughly 8-12% by Dec 31; no Dec 31 strike was found and that contract's resolution rules were not confirmed. Downside risks: attacks intensifying (47/day Nov 13-14), the town reportedly cut off by road, and this question resolving No on mere 'Assessed Russian Advances' shading.
calls.dossier:
- ISW Nov 1 2026 (via mezha.net): the rapid pace of Russia's offensive on the Dobropillia axis has yielded no significant gains; ~30 attacks/day; Russia has not consolidated any positions in the town.
- ISW Nov 11 2026: geolocated footage (Nov 10) shows a Russian advance in central Bilytske (SE of Dobropillia); Russian infiltration missions north and SE of the town, struck by Ukrainian forces; the Russian MoD claim to have seized Shylivka (SW) was refuted by a Ukrainian source.
- Ukrainian General Staff via ISW, Nov 13-14 2026: 47 assaults on the Dobropillia axis, the most since Nov 1; mechanized assaults increasing on the Dobropillia and Kostiantynivka axes.
- Suspilne, Nov 2026: an Azov officer says Russia is raising infantry assaults to meet a command promise to take all of Donetsk Oblast by year end, with almost no advances; advance of >4 km2 near Svitle and Vodianske.
- WSJ, Nov 6 2026 (question background): ~6:1 Russian manpower advantage in the sector; about a third of the Rubicon drone force deployed; Russia making some gains at high cost.
- Euromaidan Press, Sep 25 2026: ISW map showed Russian forces 10+ km from Dobropillia, despite Russian encirclement claims.
- Question background: by Nov 7 2026 ISW's assessed Russian advances were <5 km from the admin building; the town has been cut off from road transport since summer 2026.
- ISW also assesses the offensive pace is insufficient to take the fortress belt by spring 2027.
- Base-rate note: Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka and Chasiv Yar each took many months of infiltration between Russian forces reaching the outskirts and ISW assessing center control; over the class of Donbas towns of 20k+, a fall within ~6 weeks from ~5 km is uncommon.
- Market note: Polymarket has a 'Will Russia capture Dobropillia by...?' ladder (~$199K total volume); no Dec 31 2026 strike was found; its resolution rules were not verified.
- Status quo: Ukraine holds the admin building (no Russian shading on it).
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the ISW/CTP ArcGIS interactive map at 48.45985N, 37.081E on Dec 31 2026; solid pink 'Assessed Russian Advances' or 'Assessed Russian Control' = No; unshaded, infiltration areas, or 'Claimed Russian Territory' = Yes.
- Event window: a state check at Dec 31 2026 per the criteria; as of Nov 16 2026, ~45 days remain.
- Searched but not found: an ISW map reading for the building after Nov 7; a Dec 31 Polymarket strike; Manifold or Kalshi contracts on Dobropillia.
calls.reference_class: Russian offensives on defended mid-sized Donbas towns 2024-2026: share where ISW moved the town center to Russian advance/control within ~6 weeks of advances being ~5 km away

calls.reasoning: Status quo: ISW assesses no Russian control of central Dobropillia. As of Nov 7 the nearest assessed Russian advances were under 5 km from the building, and DeepState showed the first grey zone at the southern edge of town (3% of the city area). ISW Nov 15: no advance despite about 40% of all frontline engagements being in this direction. In comparable Russian assaults on fortified towns (Pokrovsk, Chasiv Yar, Toretsk), ISW took months to go from first infiltration to marking the town centre as a Russian advance; it is conservative and needs geolocated evidence, and 6.5 weeks remain. Risks: a 6:1 troop ratio, a large Rubicon drone deployment, fog limiting Ukrainian drones, and Russia's year-end Donetsk goal could cause a collapse. No matching human market: Polymarket's Dobropillia series has resolved (Nov 30 traded below 1%), and the Manifold candidates are about postwar territory.

calls.reasoning: Status quo: ISW assesses no consolidated Russian positions in Dobropillia; nearest assessed advances ~<5 km from the central admin building as of Nov 7, and ISW Nov 15 reports no advances despite ~40% of front engagements here. Reference class (Pokrovsk, Chasiv Yar, Toretsk) shows months from edge infiltration to ISW marking the town centre; only ~45 days remain and ISW requires geolocated evidence. calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the core facts (ISW Nov 1: no consolidated positions; Nov 7 map <5 km; Nov 15 no advances; WSJ 6:1 ratio; 45 days left) and land at 0.91-0.93. The factual disputes were the state of Polymarket's 'capture Dobropillia' ladder (Run 1: Mar 2027 ~43%, Run 3: <1% on all deadlines, Run 2: resolved). These accounts are incompatible and I had no web access, so I left that unsettled and did not anchor on it. Run 2's DeepState report of a southern-edge grey zone (3% of the city) is consistent with the trend but does not put Russian forces near the central building. Weighing the rest was judgment: the slow pace and ISW's conservatism outweigh the intense Russian pressure over a 6-week window, so I keep ~0.91.
